_comment: M3's labelled set. build-sequence.md asks for 'parsing accuracy acceptable on a
small labeled set'; this is it, and tests/integration/test_resume_parse_live.py is
Every résumé here is synthetic — invented people, invented employers, example.com
addresses. Nothing in this directory is anyone's real document (Part 13 rule 9 in
spirit: a fixture is committed forever).
Each fixture carries a trap on purpose. Add a fixture when a real résumé breaks the
parser in a way none of these do, and say which trap it carries.

senior_backend.pdf.trap: the clean case — single column, conventional headings, work auth stated plainly

two_column.pdf.trap: two columns — pdfminer.six is documented to interleave these line by line

career_changer.docx.trap: no Projects and no Certifications section — the shape that makes a parser requiring every section raise; also a DOCX rather than a PDF

plain.txt.trap: the no-extraction-risk baseline — if this one fails, the model or the prompt is at fault and not the converter. Two more: its CURRENT title carries no seniority word, so it exercises the tenure fallback; and it names no city at all ("Remote (GMT+1)"), so it is the fixture that proves the parser does not invent one
